open.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
Shut the door or stand in it, but don't do both. Gale's force eight off the point and the kettle's only just caught up.
cd_coastguard
Ray Sturdy. Culver lookout since '71. If you're the people Hazel rang about, you're late, and if you're not, you're lost.
miriam
He's not looked away from the window once. Neither of us has said anything worth a window yet.

passives.line: The rope on the Land Rover's tow hook is wet through and the rain's only just started. He's been down the cliff this morning.
The set's squelch is wound to the stop and the log on the desk is open at a page that says NOISE four times in one hand.

options.text: Hazel rang. We're the ones who still believe the kids.
Lost, then. Point us at the sea and we'll work the rest out.
We've read the 1973 log. We want the man who wrote it.
(Stand in the door. Let the gale in. Say nothing.)

door.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
...Shut it. All right. You can stand a blow, I'll give you that. Most of them come in sideways and talk about the view.
cd_coastguard
Hazel said you'd be odd. She didn't say odd and quiet. That's rarer.

snap.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
You've read a copy. Hazel's copy. I wrote the original and I'm not an exhibit, so sit down and ask like a person.
teddy
Twenty years of being a footnote. We just called him one to his face.

hub.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
Right. Tea's stewed, the sea's up, and I've a watch to keep. Ask it short.
hub.prompt: Ray waits with his back to the window.

options.text: Low water's in two hours. Can we get round the point under the cliff in this?
Your squelch is at the stop. What were you keeping off the speaker last night?

fail.line: Weather. It's a weather set. Mind the kettle.

options.text: You've heard a ship break up. What's at the back of that cave sounds worse. Say what it is.
We taped your nothing. Every channel. Have a listen to nothing.

static.line: He's heard it on the band tonight already. It's in his shoulders. Make him say it before the kettle does.

window.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
An hour either side of the bottom of the tide and not a minute more. Go in on the ebb, come out before it turns, and the sea won't argue.
cd_coastguard
Rope round the Land Rover, and one of you stays on the beach with a watch. I've been down this morning. It's dry to the second bend.
dale
He's just told us the second bend is where he stopped. The one who stays with the watch is the one who matters.

window_fail.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
In this? You'd be a log entry. 'Three visitors, American, last seen heading round the point.' I've written that one before, without the American.
cd_coastguard
Go and ask Hazel for the battery key. The tunnel's wet but it doesn't come in over your head.
june
He said the tunnel's wet. He didn't say where the water comes from. Two miles from the sea, that's a question.

noise.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
...A dial tone. Every channel between 156 and 162 purring like a phone off the hook, and Niton on the other side of the hill swearing their band's clean.
cd_coastguard
I wrote NOISE. You write noise and nobody rings. Twice this week, after eleven. It's only here. It's only this point.
june
Only this point. A tone that respects a hill but not a frequency. I want the tape running here tonight.

cave_sound.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
...A click. Like a dial going round a notch at a time. And three notes behind it, same three, and then the click again.
cd_coastguard
A ship breaking up sounds like something dying. This sounds like something counting. I came out faster than I went in and I'm not ashamed of it.
elijah
Counting. He's right. It isn't waiting for anything. It's keeping score.

cave_fail.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
What I heard is in my log, and my log's the Coastguard's, and you can write to Southampton.
cd_coastguard
Hazel's got the key to the battery. Hazel talks. Go and bother Hazel.
ruth
We pushed on the one thing he's frightened of, dear. Leave him his watch.

tape.speaker: cd_coastguard
lines: cd_coastguard
...That's it. That's the sound. You got it on a Woolworths cassette and I've got a set the Admiralty paid for and I put 'noise'.
cd_coastguard
Sit here after eleven. I'll leave the squelch off. If it does it again I'll sign for it this time, with the time, in ink.
teddy
A coastguard who'll sign. That's the first signature anyone's put under those children in twenty years.
